title: Majapahit
summary: Majapahit was an East Javanese state founded by Prince Vijaya after King Kertanagara died in 1292. Its prime minister Gajah Mada, virtual ruler from 1330 to 1364, brought many Indonesian islands and part of the Malay Peninsula into a tribute relationship. Its power ebbed from the late fourteenth century, and its dynasty ended in the 1520s or 1530s. UNESCO lists Trowulan as its former capital.

uncertainty.note: Start: the Library of Congress study says Kertanagara (reigned 1268-92) was killed and Prince Vijaya then established a new dynasty, with no founding year given. End: the dynasty "ended in the 1520s or 1530s".

as_recorded.value: for more than 200 years between the 13th - 15th century AD

importance.justification: A Hindu-Buddhist state whose tribute network, in the Library of Congress account, spread through much of modern Indonesia.

The LoC study says Melaka competition hastened Majapahit disintegration.
